articleTitle: A chaotic attractor from Chua's circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A chaotic attractor has been observed with an extremely simple autonomous circuit. It is third order, reciprocal and has only one nonlinear element; a 3-segment piecewise-linear resistor. The attractor appears to have interesting structures that are different from Lorenz's and Rössler's.

articleTitle: Design of linear CMOS transconductance elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Some novel circuit techniques for realizing linear CMOS tranconductance elements are proposed. The circuits discussed have superior linearity and input voltage range compared with the conventional source-coupled differential pair. Design tradeoffs are examined and computer simulation results are used to verify theoretical predictions. The results show close agreement between predicted behavior and simulated performance.

articleTitle: Optimal design of state - space digital filters by simultaneous minimization of sensitivity and roundoff noise
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The relation between a newly defined sensitivity measure and the noise power gain for scaled filters is given. By means of this relation it is shown that the necessary and sufficient condition to minimize the noise power gain is to minimize the sensitivity measure for unsealed filters. It is shown that the minimization of this sensitivity measure can be carried out without taking into account the dynamic range constraint. A procedure for the simultaneous minimization of the sensitivity measure and the noise power gain is also given.

articleTitle: Some efficient digital prefilter structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new approach to the design of low complexity FIR digital filters was presented in [1]. The essence of the method is to separate the design problem into two parts: the realization of an efficient prefilter and the design of the corresponding equalizer. This separation allows the filter designer to focus on the computational complexity issue within the simplified context of the prefilter network. In this paper, we consider the use of various digital prefilter structures. The number of possibilities for digital prefilters is unlimited, so that our treatment cannot be exhaustive. However, our study does provide a quantitative sense of the level of reduction in computational complexity that can be achieved by the use of an appropriately designed prefilter.

articleTitle: Collector amplitude modulation of the class E tuned power amplifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the class<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</tex>high-efficiency switching-mode tuned power amplifier, the RF output amplitude is almost exactly a linear function of the collector dc supply voltage, since conduction angles and wave shapes are not changed by the dc supply voltage. Thus the RF output can be amplitude-modulated by varying the dc supply voltage in accordance with desired amplitude-modulation (AM) envelope. Deviations from the ideal linear modulation characteristic are caused by: transistor saturation voltage; RF feedthrough from the driver via<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_{cb}</tex>; nonunity transmission of the ac modulating signal into the amplifier through the nonzero inductance of the collector shuntfeed RF choke; and differences in the magnitudes and delay times, of the RF transmission function through the RF output network, of three different frequencies: lower sideband, carrier, and upper sideband. Design criteria are given, to hold the modulation distortion below a limit chosen by the designer. Experimental results agree well with analytical predictions. Distortion of the modulation envelope can easily be held below 1 percent.

articleTitle: On the existence of energy function for power systems with transmission losses
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper we show that any energy (Lyapunov) function to analyze the stability of equilibrium points of systems with transmission losses would, in general, not be a continuous (with respect to transmission losses) deformation of the standard energy function used for a lossless system. This result implies that stability analysis using Lyapunov functions for systems with losses would require Lyapunov functions that are substantially different from the energy function used for lossless systems.

articleTitle: A VLSI algorithm for direct and reverse conversion from weighted binary number system to residue number system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Residue Number Systems (RNS) are proved to be useful in many applications, as for example in signal processing. In this paper, a VLSI computing architecture is proposed for converting an integer number N from the weighted binary representation into and out a residue code based on s moduli. For this architecture a possible layout is given and its complexity is evaluated in terms of area and time. Under several hypotheses on RNS parameters, constructive upper bounds ranging from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(n^{2} \log n)</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(n^{2}</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\log \log n)</tex>and from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(\log^{2} n)</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(\log n)</tex>for area and time, respectively, have been obtained for the direct conversion. On the contrary, constructive upper bounds<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A = 0(n^{2} \log n)</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T = 0(\log^{2} n)</tex>have been found independent of the formed hypotheses, for the reverse conversion.

articleTitle: Electronically controlled active-C filters and equalizers with operational transconductance amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Current-controlled filters and equalizers that employ only operational transconductance amplifiers (OTA's) and capacitors are presented. Those circuits can be integrated in bipolar technology and are characterized by good linearity between controlled parameters and their respective control currents.

articleTitle: A compact IGFET charge model
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new IGFET charge model, consistent with the recently published Compact Short-Channel IGFET Model [1], [2], is presented. It is simple, accurate, and suitable for circuit simulation applications. Charge conservation is guaranteed by using charge as the state variable. The partitioning of channel charge into drain and source components is given significant attention. This partitioning changes smoothly from 40/60 in the saturation region asymptotically to 50/50 in the triode region. The terminal charges are well behaved over all regions of operation. This charge model and its dc characteristic counterpart, derived from the same considrerations of MOS device physics, form a unified model previously unavailable.

articleTitle: Design of FIR two- dimensional digital filters by successive projections
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An iterative optimization technique based on the method of successive projections is proposed for the design of the two-dimensional (2-D) linear phase FIR digital filters. The technique is simple, fast, and compares favorably with the presently available design techniques. To illustrate the method several filters with masks up to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25 \times 25</tex>have been designed. The technique can also be used to design 1-D linear phase FIR filters.

articleTitle: 1-D models for m-D processes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper considers the local state model proposed by Givonne-Rosser Ill. It is shown that this model has a natural 1-D state variable realization which is independent of any scanning procedure. While attention is focused on the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m = 2</tex>case, extensions to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m > 2</tex>are readily available.

articleTitle: Design of 2-D separable-denominator recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a technique for finding the coefficients of a two-dimensional (2-D) recursive digital filter having a separable denominator which gives the best approximation, in the least squares sense, to a desired 2-D impulse response over a finite interval. All the coefficients in the filter are found by iteratively solving linear equations. Since the resulting filter has a separable denominator, it is easy to check the stability and the implementation is simpler. Two examples are given to illustrate the utility of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: On a fundamental property of the cross- Gramian matrix
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The cross-Gramian matrix<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W_{c0} (T)</tex>for linear single-input single-output (SISO) dynamical systems has been related to the controllability and observability Gramians via<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W^{2}_{c0}(T)= W_{c}(T)W_{0}(T)</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T= \infty</tex>. The result is now proved for any arbitrary time interval<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>, and is extended to symmetric multivariable systems which have symmetric transfer function matrices.

articleTitle: Novel floating ideal tunable FDNR simulation using current conveyors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel active-RC circuit configuration for the realization of a floating admittance<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y(s) = s^{2}D_{0}</tex>is proposed. The novelties of the scheme are realizability of ideal FDNR<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(D_{0})</tex>element using only two resistors and a capacitor, use of second-generation current conveyors (CC II) as the active elements which offer extremely low active sensitivites, no design constraint involving component matching, and tunability of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D_{0}</tex>by single resistor.

articleTitle: On the identification and design of single amplifier single resistance controlled oscillators
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Some interesting observations are made on eight recently reported single-amplifier single-resistance-controlled (SRCO) oscillators. We show that those 8 circuits can be regrouped into two families qualified as modified Deliyannis-Friend Bridge-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>and modified RC: CR dual of the Deliyannis-Friend Bridge-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>. We, furthermore, show that only two circuits need be identified and present a synthesis method which preserves the nature and value of all admittances in each circuit belonging to a given family.

articleTitle: On the design of optimal state-space realizations of second-order digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Simple design equations are derived for optimal (minimum roundoff noise) state-space realizations of second-order digital filter sections with complex poles. These relations permit easy computation of filter coefficients and unit noise gain directly from the filter transfer function. New parameters are identified that are easily computed from the transfer function, are invariant under certain frequency-scaling transformations, and which can be used to simply describe all of the design variables of optimal second-order filters, including state covariance matrix, unit noise matrix and second-order modes. The design relations are illustrated by computing the unit noise gains and eigenvalue sensitivities of optimal parallel realizations of Chebyshev lowpass filters.

articleTitle: Integrators and differentiators with current conveyors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Ideal integrators and differentiators with second generation current conveyors (CC's) as active devices have been proposed. Single-CC realization schemes are derived from a generalized approach and are shown to have marginal improvement over the conventional types, whereas, the two-CC realizations are canonical with respect to the passive components, amenable for producing independently controllable large time constants and practically insensitive to active prarmeter variation.

articleTitle: Optimum adaptive algorithms with applications to noise cancellation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new simple formulation for the choice of the optimum convergence factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>in adaptive filtering using gradient techniques is given. This leads to several optimum adaptive filtering algorithms each of which is optimum under the conditions it was derived. Several of these algorithms have been tested successfully proving their optimality and yielding faster and more accurate adaptation compared with the existing conventional algorithm CA that uses fixed or imperical<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>. Two algorithms are derived and examined here. The first, the Homogeneous Algorithm HA, results in a time varying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>which is the same for each filter but is updated at each iteration to yield optimum performance. The second, the Individual Adaptation Algorithm (IAA), has a time varying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>which is chosen suitably for each coefficient at each iteration. The performance of the HA and IAA always outperformed the CA. Computer simulations and experimental results are given which are in agreement with theory.

articleTitle: On maximally-flat linear-phase FIR filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An implementation for maximally-flat FIR filters is proposed that requires a much smaller number of multiplications than a direct form structure. The values of the multiplier coefficients in the implementation are conveniently small, and do not span a huge dynamic range, unlike in a direct form implementation.

articleTitle: Low-sensitivity recursive digital filters obtained via the delay replacement
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is proposed for synthesizing very low-sensitivity recursive digital filters on the basis of three techniques: 1) delay replacement; 2) transformation of resistance-terminated reactive ladders into digital structures; 3) multiplier scaling. The method applies to the case where the poles of the transfer function of the filter are near<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z = 1</tex>, as is the case when the sampling rate is increased. The low-sensitivity property of the resulting schemes is proved and illustrated by examples.

articleTitle: Upward topological analysis of large circuits using directed graph representation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the method of topological analysis of large LLS networks with the use of hierarchical decomposition of the network graph. It is assumed that the network is represented by a directed graph. An algorithm of upward hierarchical analysis of a partitioned graph is presented. The algorithm allows symbolic analysis of large networks with the number of elements kept as symbols practically unlimited. The computational time linearly depends on the network size. A computer program using techniques described is also presented.

articleTitle: Linear phase bandpass digital filters with variable cutoff frequencies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A low-pass-to-bandpass transformation for linear phase FIR filters is discussed. The transformed bandpass filter is implemented in a network structure in which the cutoff frequencies are controlled through two parameters. The range through which the cutoff frequencies of the transformed filter can be varied depends on the cutoff frequency and the stopband edge frequency of the prototype low-pass filter. For a given prototype filter, this range is obtained from a set of simple graphs.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient second-order digital filter sections with low roundoff noise gain
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A class of second-order recursive digital filter realizations is described that provides near-optimal roundoff noise performance, low-coefficient sensitivity, and freedom from overflow limit cycles. The number of multiplications required, per output sample, is one more than the canonical direct form realization. This class of realizations provides an attractive compromise between the computationally intensive optimal realization and the finite-word-sensitive direct form. Explicit design procedures are provided, and a numerical design example is presented that illustrates the near-optimal performance of this new class of realizations.

articleTitle: Time-shared switched-capacitor ladder filters insensitive to parasitic effects
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The time-sharing technique can be applied to LDI clocked differential SC ladder filters, which exhibit full insensitivity to parasitic effects. In turn, the time-sharing foresees a reduced number of the operational amplifiers with respect to conventional SC ladder schemes, which could allow to save die area and power consumption in an integrated circuit. The cross-talk mechanism is also compensated in differential time-shared stages. As an example, the design of a fifth-order elliptic TS-SC ladder filter is given and numerical results are furnished.

articleTitle: Applications of a direct-transfer SC integrator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A direct-transfer switched-capacitor (SC) integrator is one in which each input voltage sample is added directly to the output, instead of being ratioed through an input capacitor. The property of ensured unity-gain can be taken advantage of in a simplified, low-sensitivity first-order all-pass, and in a unity-gain buffer.

articleTitle: Bifurcation diagram for a piecewise-linear circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The bifurcation diagram of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R-L</tex>-Diode circuit driven by a sinusoidal voltage source is computed. The model of the diode is piecewise linear. Qualitatively, the same phenomena have been obtained as for the previously published computer simulation with the conventional junction diode model.

articleTitle: Nonlinear distortion analysis of p-i-n diode attenuators using Volterra series representations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An application of Volterra series to the analysis of a network with nonlinear elements represented by Volterra series is presented. For the equivalent circuit of this network, the outputs of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>th-order nonlinear sources are given in the frequency domain. The model of the p-in diode in a form of the Volterra series, which was proposed earlier by the author, is implemented and the results of the analysis are used to derive the cross-modulation coefficient for a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\pi</tex>-type attenuator with three p-in diodes. Computation results are compared with those obtained from measurements.

articleTitle: A general property of the transformation matrices associated with the n-variable bilinear transformation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: By applying the bilinear transformation to a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-variable polynomial, with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 1</tex>, one arrives at a rational function, the zeros of which represent the "transformed polynomial." Let<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>be the matrix relating the coefficients of the original polynomial to those of the transformed polynomial. It is shown that the matrix<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>has a unique property, namely,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q^{2} = kl</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>is a positive constant which is explicitly derived for the various cases discussed, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</tex>is the unit matrix of the pertinent order.

articleTitle: Oscillator with odd- symmetrical characteristics eliminates low-frequency noise sidebands
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Low-frequency noise in an oscillator normally produces two LF noise sidebands around the center frequency<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f_{0}</tex>of the oscillator. It was shown experimentally that these noise sidebands can be eliminated by using an oscillator circuit with an odd-symmetrical characteristic. A simple theory based on the van der Pol approach to oscillators can explain the observed effects.

articleTitle: Fast design of direct and ladder Wiener filters with linear phase
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the problem of computationally efficient design of finite impulse response Wiener filters with linear phase is considered. For stationary signals these filters are determined by the solution of normal systems of equations whose associated matrix has a Toeplitz-plus (or minus)-Hankel structure. A fast order recursive algorithm for solving these normal equations is developed. The componentparts of this scheme are the Levinson algoritun and an elegant relationship connecting Wiener filters and Wiener filters with linear phase. Finally, it is shown that the well known two multiplier lattice structure introduced by Itakura and Saito can be used in a natural way to realize a ladder Wiener filter with linear phase.

articleTitle: On selectivity properties of discrete-time linear networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A definition of the quality factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>and the resonant angle<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\theta_{0}</tex>for discrete-time networks is presented. The definitions are based on the bilinear transform. Using this transform, the selectivity properties for discrete-time networks, such as switched capacitor (SC) and digital filters, are consistent with analog networks. Expressions for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\theta_{0}</tex>in terms of polar coordinate parameters<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\theta_{p}</tex>for a complex-conjugate pole pair and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x_{1}</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x_{2}</tex>for real-axis poles are given as well as the inverse relations. Canonic expressions for generic forms of a biquadratic function are also given. Finally, an accurate method for measurement of the parameters in second-order SC-filters and digital filters implemented in software is described.

articleTitle: Block floating-point distributed filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Distributed filters have been shown to offer an impressive complexity-throughput tradeoff. In this correspondence, a precision improvement is made in distributed filtering using block floating-point arithmetic. Performance improvement is predicted and verified using numerical experimentation. Using this scheme, additional distributed filter precision can be obtained.

articleTitle: A pipelined recursive residue number system digital filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The well-known advantages of pipelining as applied to Finite Impulse Response (FIR) Residue Number System (RNS) arithmetic digital filters is extended to the important area of Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) digital filters through a new technique based on augmentation of the IIR transfer function. Through this technique, pipelined IIR filters based on RNS Read-Only-Memory (ROM) table look-up techniques can be designed which offer throughput rates equal to the table look-up time of the ROM's. This high-speed realization can be achieved even though the recursive filter algorithm requires multiple delays in realizing the output of the filter. For the example of a typical second-order IIR filter, the pipelined structure represents a five-fold increase in speed over standard techniques. Higher order realizations will yield proportionately higher speed improvements. Although the new technique does increase somewhat the hardware complexity of the filter, the increase in speed will often justify the additional hardware. The paper discusses the basic technique, stability considerations, and hardware realizations.

articleTitle: A generalized bandwidth estimation theory for feedback amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A procedure for quickly determining the 3-dB bandwidth of active low-pass networks is derived and exemplified. The procedure is useful for realistic assessment of topological adequacy in advance of extensive computer-based studies. Unlike other methods of bandwidth estimation, the method presented in this paper explicitly accounts for the effects of finite transmission zeros and the critical parameter of an embedded feedback loop.

articleTitle: On the elimination of constant-input limit cycles in digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A theorem is proved which establishes sufficient conditions that will ensure freedom from constant-input limit cycles in a general digital-filter structure in which zero-input limit cycles can be eliminated. The theorem is then applied to a specific digital biquad which realizes simultaneously all the standard second-order transfer functions.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of limit cycles in nonlinear feedback systems using describing functions: Improved results
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: We formulate and establish a rigorous stability analysis for limit cycles for a large class of nonlinear feedback systems. Our approach uses the classical sinusoidal-input describing function and the theory of integral manifolds. The present results constitute an improvement of earlier results by the present authors. We demonstrate the usefulness of the present results by means of a specific example.

articleTitle: Combined error at the output of two-dimensional recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The noise properties of two-dimensional (2-D) recursive digital filters, caused by finite register lengths, are considered. A combined error model is proposed, which takes into account three sources of error; roundoff accumulation, coefficient quantization, and input quantization. A statistical approach is used, in the space domain, which allows the computation of the statistics of the errors at the filter output.

articleTitle: The nonlinear analog fault diagnosis scheme of Wu, Nakajima, Wey, and Saeks in the tableau context
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Tradeoffs between passive sensitivity, output voltage swing, and total capacitance in biquadratic SC filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Design guidelines for biquadratic SC filters taking into consideration passive sensitivity, output voltage swing, and total capacitance area are described. In this paper, we discuss the tradeoffs between these three parameters. A popular SC topology with additional positive feedback is used to illustrate the tradeoffs involved in the design of SC filters.

articleTitle: Wave digital biquads derived from RC-active configurations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general method for deriving digital-filter structures from corresponding<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>-active configurations is presented. The method is then used to derive digital-filter structures from various low-sensitivity<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>-active configurations such as the three-amplifier state-variable biquad, and the corresponding summing four-amplifier biquad. The new digital structures are found to have the salient features of the reference configurations. For example, the structures based on the summing four-amplifier biquad embody the simultaneous realization of a variety of filter transfer functions, namely, a low-pass, a bandpass, and a general biquadratic transfer function. In addition, it is shown that in these structures, limit cycles can be eliminated by using a known technique based on magnitude truncation.

articleTitle: Exact synthesis of bandpass switched- capacitor LDI ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Exact design techniques are given for the design of leapfrog switched-capacitor bandpass filters using lossless discrete integrator (LDI)-type building blocks. No assumptions are made regarding the sampling rate except that of satisfying the sampling theorem, and only strays-insensitive circuits are employed. The design techniques derive from a prototype filter employing unit elements. The filters have no lumped counterpart, and cannot be obtained from lumped filters by a transformation or otherwise. They also retain the optimum sensitivity properties of the corresponding passive distributed filters.

articleTitle: Broad-band matching of multiport networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Given an arbitrary passive, non-Foster impedance,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n - 1</tex>resistances and the preassigned transducer power-gain characteristics, necessary and sufficient conditions are given for the existence of a lossless reciprocal equalizer which when terminated in the loads achieves the preassigned transducer power-gain characteristics.

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor realization of FIR filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Finite impulse response (FIR) filters can be realized without multipliers and delays by delta modulating the input signal [5]. In this letter, we describe a stray-insensitive switched-capacitor (SC) implementation of such delta modulation FIR filters.

articleTitle: Series - parallel graphs and depth-first search trees
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Series-parallel graphs play a significant role in the analysis and synthesis of electrical networks, communication networks, and switching circuits. On the other hand, due to their very tractable structure, a number of algorithmic problems which are NP-complete for arbitrary graphs can be efficiently solved for the special case of series-parallel graphs, see some recent results in [7]. In another recent work, Shinoda et al. [6] have shown that series-parallel graphs can be completely characterized by a property of their spanning trees. They proved, that every spanning tree of a series-parallel graph<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>is a depth-first search (or DFS) tree of a 2-isomorphic copy of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>. The proof in [6] is, however, existential. The purpose of this note is to provide a constructive proof of this property. We present a procedure which for a given series-parallel graph<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>and its spanning tree<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>, produces a 2-isomorphic copy<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G'</tex>of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>such that the edges of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>generate in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G'</tex>a DFS tree of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G'</tex>. Our considerations are entirely based on the classical constructive definition of series-parallel graphs and the Duffin's characterization, unlike the work [6], where several other characterizations of these graphs are utilized. We refer the reader to Chen [1] and Harary [4] for graph-theoretic terms not defined here.

articleTitle: Kirchhoff's laws and Tellegen's theorem for networks and continuous media
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the relation between network theory and quasistatic field theory. The fundamental orthogonality relations (Tellegen's theorem for circuits-a generalization of it given here for fields) are derived by parallel routes for the two disciplines. To illustrate that this parallel development can produce new insights, a standard integral theorem from vector calculus suggests a novel formulation of Tellegen's theorem for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>-terminal elements.

articleTitle: Submarking reachability of marked graphs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Reachability of marked graphs is generalized to that with respect to any subgraph of the marked graph. It is shown that the existence of a minimum firing count vector satisfying a set of equality and inequality constraints is equivalent to the submarking reachability. A necessary and sufficient condition is presented for the existence of the minimum firing count vector together with its constructing algorithm. The result can be applied to the problem of finding the shortest firing sequence which arises in practical sequential control problems.

articleTitle: A switched-capacitor multiplier/divider with digital and analog outputs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel switched-capacitor circuit is proposed for digital multiplication and division. The inputs (two binary numbers) are first converted to analog charges by means of binary-weighted capacitor arrays. Then, multiplication or division is performed between these charges to provide the product or ratio in the form of an analog voltage. Finally, the resulting analog voltage is converted to a binary number by successiveapproximation analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. An error analysis using the charge conservation equation has shown that a 10-bit accuracy is obtainable using this technique with presently available MOS technology. An experimental circuit was built and tested. The results confirmed the principles of operation.

articleTitle: New second-order digital filter sections without limit cycles
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Limit cycles in recursive digital filters can be avoided along various ways. Wave digital filtering (WDF) and controlled rounding are two deterministic limit-cycle suppressing tools that are in current use. In this paper two novel second-order sections are derived from the foregoing principles that use only one quantizer with a magnitude truncation characteristic. Limit-cycle suppression in these sections applies to a broader class of input signals than in previous solutions: stability is guaranteed for the zero-input, constant-input, and alternating-input situation. More generally, all periodic excitations with periods not longer than two are admitted. As a characteristic feature the new sections contain loops which do not require quantization, because only multiplications with integer factors are involved.

articleTitle: Pole assignment of SISO system using dynamic compensation with prespecified poles
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new method for pole assignment of a class of SISO systems using dynamic compensator with prescribed poles is presented. This method will always yield a stable dynamic compensator and is especially useful for designing power system stabilizer.

articleTitle: A study on the properties of multi-dimensional Fourier transforms
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A parametric representation of a composite operation consisting of transformation, conjugation, and modulation suitable for the study of the properties of multi-dimensional<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(m-D)</tex>Fourier transforms is developed. A class of properties of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m-D</tex>Fourier transforms is established using these parameters.

articleTitle: A stability inequality for nonlinear discrete-time systems with slope-restricted nonlinearity
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel frequency domain criterion is presented for the absolute stability of Lure type single-input single-output discrete-time systems with slope-restricted nonlinearity.

articleTitle: A novel SC oscillator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Synthesis of higher order nonlinear circuit elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Higher and mixed-order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-port circuit elements were introduced recently to provide a logically complete formulation for nonlinear circuit theory. In this paper, higher order mutators are defined and used to synthesize these elements. The class of all higher order mutators is shown to form a group under cascade interconnections. Each mutator is realized using only linear capacitors, linear inductors and linear controlled sources. An upper bound on each type of element needed to realize a mutator is also given. Each higher or mixed-order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-port element is realized by cascading appropriate mutators across each port of a nonlinear<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-port resistor. Our main theorem shows that any higher or mixed-order nonlinear<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-port element with a constitutive relation defined on a compact set can be realized using linear capacitors, inductors, and controlled sources, and 2 -terminal nonlinear resistors.

articleTitle: An algorithm for a 2-D continued fraction inversion
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper indicates that the one-shot algorithm proposed recently by John and Parthasarathy for inverting a one-dimensional (1-D) continued fraction can be extended to the two-dimensional (2-D) case by merely using polynomial coefficient array (PCA) to represent a 2-D polynomial.

articleTitle: Comments on "A fast procedure to design equiripple minimum-phase FIR filters"
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that the approximation problem for minimum-phase FIR filters with arbitrary specifications on the attenuation can be solved by a method published in [3] although that method is based on the same idea of that developed in the above \footnote[1]{paper}, it is simpler and also easier to apply.

articleTitle: The convergence of Volterra series for nonlinear networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Sufficient conditions are derived for the existence of the convergent Volterra series representation of nonlinear time-invariant networks. The estimate of the radius of convergence is given.

articleTitle: The driving-point immittances of infinite cascades of nonlinear three-terminal networks: II-Nonuniform cascades
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: That nonuniform infinite cascades of linear resistive three-terminal networks can have driving-point immittances has been known for a long time, but this has not been established for nonlinear networks. This work does so. It thereby extends a prior analysis that established the existence of nonlinear characteristic immittances for uniform cascades. For the special case of nonuniform infinite ladder networks, it is shown herein that, when the nonlinear shunting conductances and series resistances are continuous, positive for positive arguments, negative for negative arguments, zero at the origin, monotonic near the origin, and uniformly bounded away from zero on any compact interval not containing the origin, then the ladder network possesses driving-point immittances, which are nonlinear curves in the voltage-current plane. Our results for nonuniform cascades of three-terminal networks employ generalizations of these monotonicity and boundedness requirements.

articleTitle: A frequency- domain inequality for stochastic power flow in linear networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the frequency-domain characterization of stochastic signals in linear time-invariant distributed networks. A new general relation is derived. The average power flow at each frequency from one source to another through a lossless coupling network is shown to obey an inequality related to the second law of thermodynamics. The sources can be essentially any stationary random signal or noise processes; in particular, they need not represent thermal noise. In this sense the inequality is quite general. Proofs are based on standard techniques from the theory of linear circuits and random signals: thermodynamic concepts are used only for motivation and interpretation.

articleTitle: High- speed PLL and frequency synthesizer for low frequencies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Conventional phase-locked loops (PLL's) lack speed, because ordinary phase comparators cannot achieve time-continuous phase detection, introducing equivalent time delays into the loops. This paper presents a PLL reconstructed to derive time-optimal responses. First, VCO's and filters are replaced by time-discrete ones, eliminating the stability problem caused by the time delay. Second, period rather than frequency is employed as the controlled variable for utilizing digital phase comparators as linear time comparators. A prototype consisting of about 20 IC's is tested.

articleTitle: Numerical solution of the Lyapunov equation for narrow-band digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The quantization noise generated by a digital filter can be analyzed via the solution of the Lyapunov equation<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K = AKA^{T} + bb^{T}</tex>corresponding to the filter's state variable description. A method given by Mullis and Roberts [1] for the solution of the Lyapunov equation is noted for its speed of implementation, but its applicability is limited to filters with wide bandwidths because of numerical accuracy. A method of extending this algorithm to narrowband filters is presented. It uses a transformation which was also presented by Mullis and Roberts. The transformation distorts the frequency response of the filters and improves the numerical accuracy of the solution of the Lyapunov equation. The development given here is restricted to low-pass or high-pass filters, but it can be extended to bandpass filters.

articleTitle: Symbolic network function generation via discrete Fourier transform
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new method of symbolic network function generation is presented. The method is based upon the theory of the discrete Fourier transform and not restricted in its application to any particular type of network analysis or network configuration. It is particularly attractive when the number of symbolic variables to be handled is not large.

articleTitle: The solution of ill-scaled circuit equations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Due to the wide spread of element values and differing dimensions of quantities appearing in linear systems describing circuits, the systems can often become quite ill-scaled. Commonly used pivoting strategies can fail badly in such cases. It is pointed out that an accurate way to solve these ill-scaled systems is by iterative improvement in single precision.

articleTitle: Low multiplier coefficient sensitivity block digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Block ladder filters, based upon a ladder analog, are developed. A general procedure for removing delay free loops from digital filters is presented. Using the procedure, vector delay free loops of block ladder filters are eliminated. The multiplier coefficient sensitivities of the resulting block ladder based filters are considerably better than the corresponding sensitivities of previously developed block filters.

articleTitle: A frequency-domain evaluation of multiple-nonlinearity systems exhibiting jump-resonance responses
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A generalized two-nonlinearity feedback system is used to develop a numerical sequence capable of fully depicting all features of acuminating jump-resonance characteristics. This is achieved by recognizing the importance of the shape of the response of the input error signal at a nonlinear element. The curve is traced by iterating on the system equation and the describing-function integral while judiciously adjusting step sizes in accordance with the contour. Complete amplitude and phase responses can hence be extrapolated and critical-jump-resonance conditions predicted. Practical verification is provided by a simple bandpass active-filter circuit.

articleTitle: On the sensitivity analysis of linear time-invariant singular systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this contribution the problem of sensitivity analysis of singular systems is considered. Appropriate formulas for the determination of the changes that the main features of the transfer function undergo due to the disturbances of the system's parameters are presented. These formulas are useful to the analysis as well as to the synthesis, since they give directly all the necessary information about the influence of the parameter changes to the system's behavior.

articleTitle: A simultaneous frequency and time-domain approximation method for discrete-time filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A simultaneous frequency- and time-domain approximation method for discrete-time filters is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, transfer function coefficients are divided into two subsets,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{1}</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{2}</tex>, which are employed for optimizing a time response and a frequency response, respectively. Frequency and time responses are optimized through the iterative Chebyshev approximation method and a method of solving linear equations, respectively. At the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>th iteration step, the maximum frequency response error, which appeared at the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(r - 1)</tex>th step, is minimized, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{2}^{(r- 1)}</tex>becomes<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{2}^{(r)})\cdot X_{1}^{(r)}</tex>is obtained from linear equations including<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{2}^{(r)}</tex>as a constant. The frequency response at the rth step is evaluated using the above obtained<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{1}^{(r)}</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{2}^{(r)}</tex>. This means the optimum time response is always guaranteed in the frequency-response approximation procedure. A design example of a symmetrical impulse response shows the new approach is more efficient than conventional methods from the filter order reduction viewpoint.

articleTitle: A technique for the efficient generation of projections for error correcting residue codes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A concept called biased addition is proposed as a technique to simplify modular addition when the modulus is a large integer. Then it is shown that biased addition can be used in a residue number system (RNS) to generate a full set of projections as required for RNS error detection and correction. Application of biased addition simplifies the network structure of an RNS error checker so that the resulting structure is more attractive for VLSI implementation.

articleTitle: Comments on "Suppression of Limit Cycles in Digital filters designed with One Magnitude-Truncation Quantizer
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Shorted operators and the identification problems-The real case
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions under which a real symmetric nonnegative definite matrix can be uniquely determined from the knowledge of a finite number of its shorted versions.

articleTitle: Existence criteria for dc solutions of nonlinear networks which involve the independent sources
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: New theorems are presented showing how the location and value of independent sources can be used in assessing the existence of a solution for the dc equations of a very general class of nonlinear networks. The application of the theory to bipolar transistor circuits is specifically considered, and an example is given using a simple differential amplifier circuit.

articleTitle: A two's complement overflow limit cycle free digital filter structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Liapunov analysis is used to design a second-order digital incremental computer structure which is suitable for implementation by a sequentially executed program which is free of autonomous two's complement overload limit cycles.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Nonlinear One-Port Resistor Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper considers one-port resistor networks constructed from two-terminal resistors that are both passive and strictly locally passive. The results concern the global sensitivity of the terminal behavior of such networks to variations in the individual resistors. In contrast to the linear case, there are conditions under which replacing one element by a "larger" resistance will decrease the apparent resistance of the entire network at some operating point. Circuit examples are provided, and conditions under which the network resistance will and cannot decrease are derived.

articleTitle: FIR low-pass filter design using parametric filter technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a new design method for finite impulse response (FIR) filters. FIR low-pass filters which have quasi-equiripple characteristics in the stopband and arbitrary ones in the passband are designed. Applying the parametric filter design technique, the stopband zeros are given in the closed form. Hence, only passband zeros are iteratively approximated to shape passband characteristics. This method can be applied for both the minimum and the linear phase cases.

articleTitle: A simple predistortion technique for active filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This article deals with the predistortion of active-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>filters to compensate for the accountable nonideal performance of the operational amplifiers (OA's). In particular, the predistortion attempts to compensate the effect of the finite gain-bandwidth product (GB) of the OA's. This method can be used for circuits consisting of any number of OA's. The method realizes not only the specified pole frequency<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_{\rho}</tex>and pole<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q_{\rho}</tex>as some other methods do, but also the exact gain requirement at a specified frequency of importance. In specific examples, it will also be shown how to choose the parameters in the network to attain minimum pole sensitivity due to the GB's of the OA's, while predistortion is achieved. This method is simple enough that the design of most second-order active-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>filters can be implemented in a programmable calculator.

articleTitle: Markov parameter characterization of the strict positive real problem
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Suppose that a rational function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z(s)</tex>is defined by a Laurent series, the coefficients of which are known. Several criteria are given in terms of these coefficients (the Markov parameters of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z(s)</tex>) to ensure that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Re Z(j \omega) > 0</tex>for all real<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega</tex>. The criteria are defined by using a Cauchy index formulation of the ratio of two rational functions, and they are of three types-involving a Routh-like table with first two rows initialized using the coefficients, and Hurwitz and Bezout matrices with entries which are the coefficients themselves, or integral expressions in the coefficients. The matrix positive real property is also investigated.

articleTitle: Invertibility of 2-D systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper is addressed to the invertibility of 2-D multivariable systems. Algebraic structure of the ring of 2-D transfer functions is identified and used for the inversion of 2-D transfer matrices. These results are largely true for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N-D</tex>systems also.

articleTitle: Slew-induced distortion of single-amplifier active filters using the gain-sensitivity product concept
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Volterra-Wiener series is used to obtain an analytical formula for slew-induced distortion (SID) in single-amplifier active filters. It is shown that the relative change of the transfer function caused by SID depends on the parameters of the operational amplifier (OA) and on the method of frequency compensation applied to it. This change also depends on the transfer function to be realized, on the amplitude of the input signal and on the gain-sensitivity product (GSP). It is shown that reducing the GSP also reduces the SID. The corresponding relationship was verified experimentally.

articleTitle: A theorem on general LC-R ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that any real rational function with arbitrary zeros and pure imaginary poles, all preassigned except for a factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p^{r}</tex>in either the numerator or denominator, is the characteristic function of a filter which may be realized by a transformerless, inductance, capacitance ladder terminated in resistance if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>is sufficiently great.

articleTitle: On the measurement of quantization noise in digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Quantization noise in digital filters caused by magnitude truncationi exhibits a rather strong correlation with the main signal. Therefore, such noise signals are appropriately considered as sums of completely correlated and completely uncorrelated components. The first component can be interpreted as a slight change of the linear transmission characteristic of the filter whereas the second part reflects the genuinely nonlinear properties induced by quantization. Results of measurements are given; these show that the latter part accounts for a relatively small percentage of the total noise. The separation of noise components also applies to controlled rounding which is shown to be reducible to magnitude truncation.

articleTitle: Composite amplifier structures for use in active RC biquads
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The use of composite amplifiers in active filters is assessed in terms of their ability to reduce the sensitivity of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_{0}</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>to the amplifier gain-bandwidth product. A general expression is developed for the determination of such shifts in an MMFB (Delyannis) filter utilizing composite amplifiers of the third order.

articleTitle: A method for synthesizing transfer functions containing several variable parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method of synthesizing multivariable transfer functions by active-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>networks using state space methods. Multivariable transfer functions are functions of the complex angular frequency s together with several variable parameters<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Lambda_{i}</tex>, which are independent of time and frequency, but which can be changed continuously and independently. We introduce some special classes of multivariable transfer functions which can be realized with the minimal or almost the minimal number of elements.

articleTitle: A simple algorithm for the determination of a Hurwitz polynomial from its squared magnitude on the imaginary axis
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The paper presents a new algorithm for the determination of a real Hurwitz polynomial from its squared magnitude on the imaginary axis. The algorithm is based on an optimal property and does not use polynomial root extraction except when the location of some roots becomes self-evident.

articleTitle: Bounds on the tolerance sensitivity of resistive networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Abstruct -For the general class of resistive networks, lower bounds are derived on the summed absolute and squared element sensitivities of any dimensionless network function. As an application example, these results are used to obtain a lower bound on the linearity performance of digital-to-analog converters.

articleTitle: Comments on "Decision Methods and Realizations os 2-D Digital Filters Using Minimum Number of Delay Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Repeated convolutions of Butterworth-filtered spectra
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: For a low-pass<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-pole Butterworth filtered spectrum, repeated convolutions are derived in a closed form. Repeated convolution of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>results when a signal is convolved with itself<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>times. The derivation is based on the "convolution-multiplication" property of the Fourier transform. The results are useful in determining the FM spectra of Butterworth filtered Gaussian processes.

articleTitle: Design of active RC filters simulating node equations of LC filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An active<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>filter design approach based on the simulation of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LC</tex>filter is proposed. In this approach, if node equations of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LC</tex>filter are given, an active<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>structure is obtained which is described by the same equations. Then, the technique to decrease the number of operational amplifiers (OA's) is considered. The effect of gain-bandwidth products of the OA's used and that of changes in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>elements are discussed. For the design example, a fifth-order bandpass filter was selected. The experimental result showed good agreement with the theory.

articleTitle: Finite gain - bandwidth product effects on a pair of pseudo-N-path SC filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A detailed analysis of two novel SC pseudo-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>-path filters [3], [4] are presented to determine the effects of their transfer functions due to the op amp gain-bandwidth product (GB). To appreciate the difference between the two filters,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</tex>-plane root locus plots as a function of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GB/f_{c}</tex>are presented.

articleTitle: On numerical computation of functions related to transient response of capacitively loaded coaxial cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper describes efficient algorithms for numerical computation of two inverse Laplace transforms related to transient analysis of a skin-effect lossy coaxial cable loaded with a resistance shunted by a capacitance.

articleTitle: Optimum weighting functions in delay equalization
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The choice of the weighting function is an important factor in delay equilization. This paper presents a numerical approach to find the weighting function that yields a delay that is optimum in the sense of minimizing the power in echoes produced by a nearly equiripple (least squares) or equiripple (minimax) delay function. The approach employs a line search to find the optimum weighting function and the corresponding all-pass sections parameters.

articleTitle: New digital notch filter structures with low coefficient sensitivity
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: For narrow-band digital notch filters, poles are near the unit circle. Also, when the sampling rate is increased, the poles approach the point<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z = + 1</tex>. The usual realizations of digital notch filters are highly sensitive to coefficient quantization. Three new digital notch filter structures are proposed, and their coefficient sensitivities are derived.

articleTitle: Improved z plane polynomial interpolative analysis of switched-capacitor networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The accuracy of interpolated polynomials in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</tex>is considerably improved using a transformed sampling plane and the FFT. This is further enhanced when the transformation is coupled with partitioned polynomial interpolation. One solution to the problem of over-interpolation also follows.

articleTitle: A unified approach to root distribution with respect to parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Root distribution of real coefficient polynomials with respect to conic subregions in the complex plane, is determined by a standard half-plane test on a transformed polynomial. A unified approach to derive the pertinent transformation for a given conic curve by using its description in polar coordinates, is described. Specific transformations and root distribution criteria are given for a left parabola, a symmetric ellipse and a horizontal hyperbola. Examples are provided.

articleTitle: Corrected gain formulas
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Graphical design of multistage feedback amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a semi-analytical graphical technique for stabilizing an initial unstable feedback amplifier by the addition of passive circuit components. The stabilized amplifier can be chosen to have a Butterworth, Bessel, or critically damped transfer function, as desired. Its bandwidth is restricted to somewhat less than the transistor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f_{T}</tex>'s so that the transistors can be adequately represented by a hybrid-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\pi</tex>or other rational model. The technique is applied to the design of a low-noise fiber-optic receiver front end capable of driving a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50-\Omega</tex>load, with the main feedback loop around the whole amplifier.

articleTitle: A pole/zero prewarping procedure in SC filter design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: A distributional treatment of linear time-invariant system response to inputs with left-unbounded support
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Harmonic retrieval by FIR digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new algorithm is proposed for determining the FIR filter for estimating the frequencies of a process consisting of sinusoids in white noise. The algorithm is based on an extensive use of the constrained predictor and is characterized by a very fast convergence.

articleTitle: Canonical forms and strictly positive real functions for discrete multivariable systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we show that, for the discrete multivariable systems, the solution of the Lyapunov equation in the controllable canonical form transforms a companion matrix to another companion matrix. We also show that the first (last)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>columns of the inverse of this solution matrix, where the block size is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m \times m</tex>, give the left (right) matrix fraction decomposition of a strictly positive real function.

articleTitle: CAD modeling of three-terminal piecewise-linear device characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The purpose of this work is to construct a circuit analysis model synthesizing piecewise-linear characteristics of a three terminal device, using only two-terminal piecewise-linear resistors together with linear controlled sources. The model is based on representing the function, to be modeled, by a finite amount of tabulated data.

articleTitle: On the noise figure of weak signal receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A signal transmission system can be modeled as a system terminated in a reactive load<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_{0}</tex>driven by a source with an internal resistance<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{0}</tex>via an intermediate two-port network. If<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H(s)</tex>is the source-to-load voltage transfer function, a very simple expression for the maximum value of the integral<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |H(j \omega)|^{2} d \omega</tex>is given. Using this value and under the condition that an active device with low input conductance is used in the front stage of a receiver, the overall noise figure of the input stage is found to be<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F = 1+4C_{0} R_{n} B</tex>. Therefore, by using small<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_{0}</tex>'s we can manage to make the noise figure quite small at rather large wide bands<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</tex>.

articleTitle: A further asymptotic estimate of the amplitude for the two-parameter Scott - Murata oscillator and a similar estimate for a three-parameter oscillator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: For the two-parameter Scott-Murata oscillator, an estimate of the asymptotic amplitude depending only on the parameter representing the input-output characteristic has been carried out by Ceschia in a previous paper. Here, some refinements of that estimate have been given, setting out explicitly the dependence of the amplitude on the other parameter. Following a similar method a new asymptotic estimate of the amplitude for a three-parameter oscillator is also reported.

articleTitle: A canonical form for lossless multiport transmission lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The propagation of TEM waves on a reciprocal<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-port lossless nonuniform transmission line, with absolutely continuous characteristic impedance and locally equal wavefront velocities in each port, is described in this note by a canonical system of wave equations. The essential feature of this canonical system is an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \times n</tex>local reflection coefficient which generalizes the notion of a reflection coefficient for a single-port line. The reflection coefficient characterizes the local scattering behavior at any point on the line, and is unique up to a constant orthogonal transformation.

articleTitle: Direct solution of a class of solid state power converters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A certain class of power converters exhibits linear periodic time varying characteristics. This paper investigates an approximate direct solution of the steady-state operating point for this type of system. The solution is computationaly efficient, and is readily applied to complex systems.

articleTitle: Comments on "The Effects of Small Noise on Implicitly Defined Nonlinear Dynamical systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Calculation of quantization noise at non-storage nodes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The calculation of digital filter quantization noise can be facilitated through the solution of the Lyapunov equation<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">AKA^{T} + bb^{T}=K</tex>[1]. This method, however, only includes the contributions from the quantization which occurs at the inputs to time delays, that is, at the "storage nodes" of the filter. This letter shows how the method can be extended to include the contributions at the other nodes, the "signal nodes."

articleTitle: Bifurcation of periodic responses in forced dynamic nonlinear circuits: Computation of bifurcation values of the system parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the computer-aided experimental analysis of dynamic nonlinear circuits, the determination of the bifurcation value of system parameters for various types of periodic response is one of the central problems. A bifurcation diagram composed by the sets of bifurcation values exhibits various nonlinear phenomena, such as the coexistence of several periodic responses which are correlated with the jump and hysteresis behaviors, the frequency entrainment, the appearance of quasi-periodic responses and chaotic states, etc. In engineering application the bifurcation diagram can be used for designing dynamic nonlinear circuit with prescribed characteristics. In this paper, we present some computational algorithms which determine the bifurcation values of periodic responses. Our algorithms are based on the geometric approach of ordinary differential equations. Newton's method is effectively used for finding the bifurcation value. The Jacobian matrix is evaluated by the solutions of variational equations. Numerical examples for the second-order systems are illustrated. Some global properties of bifurcation sets of periodic responses are discussed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear programming without computation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Using the Kuhn-Tucker conditions from mathematical programming theory, a canonical nonlinear programming circuit for simulating general nonlinear programming problems has been developed. This circuit is canonical in the sense that its topology remains unchanged and that it requires only a minimum number of 2-terminal nonlinear circuit elements. Rather than solving the problem by iteration using a digital computer, we obtain the answer by setting up the associated nonlinear programming circuit and measuring the node voltages. In other words, the nonlinear programming circuit is simply a special purpose analog computer containing a repertoire of nonlinear function building blocks. To demonstrate the feasibility and advantage of this approach, several circuits have been built and measured. In all cases, the answers are obtained almost instantaneously in real time and are accurate to within 3 percent of the exact answers.

articleTitle: Frequency-domain analysis of nonlinear circuits driven by multi-tone signals
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
